```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Global programs are sparse sets of genes that are jointly associated with a
sparse set of trans variants. The workflow has two steps:

1. `r_transcca()` identifies programs from variant-gene association
   statistics, supplied as a `data_list` in the transBoost format.
2. `transmap_global()` turns the program gene loadings into program
   phenotypes.

`transcca_null()`, `transcca_pvalue()` and `transcca_plot()` compare the
programs with a simulated null distribution.

```{r}
library(transmap)
data(transmap_example)
z <- transmap_example$z   # 150 variants x 60 genes
dim(z)
```

## Building W from a data list

The statistics are passed as a named list, as in transBoost's `data.list`.
`w_construction()` turns the list into the variant-by-gene matrix $W$ that
transCCA decomposes; for z-scores $W = Z / \sqrt{N - 2 + Z^2}$:

```{r}
data_list <- list(Z = z, N = transmap_example$n)
W <- w_construction(data_list)
attr(W, "input")
```

The list holds one of these sets of elements (variants in rows, genes in
columns):

| `data_list` | $W$ |
|---|---|
| `Z`, `N` | $Z / \sqrt{N - 2 + Z^2}$; with `MAF` (and `sdY`) rescaled to the effect scale |
| `Beta` | `Beta`; with `MAF` (and `sdY`) rescaled to the effect scale |
| `Beta`, `N` + `Pvalue`, `Z` or `seBeta` | `Beta` scaled by each variant's genotype scale estimated from the summary statistics |
| `log2FC`, `N1`, `N0` | $\sqrt{N_1 N_0} / (N_1 + N_0) \cdot \log_2 FC$ |
| `G`, `E` (individual-level) | $G^\top E / N$ |
| `Sigma_GE` | used as is |

Adding `Sigma_GG` and/or `Sigma_EE` whitens $W$ by the variant and gene
correlation, $\Sigma_{GG}^{-1/2} W \Sigma_{EE}^{-1/2}$; with `G` and `E`,
`"insample"` uses the sample covariance.

`exclude` is a logical matrix with the dimension of $W$; `TRUE` entries are
set to zero before whitening. A common use is to mask variant-gene pairs on
the same chromosome so that only trans associations drive the programs:

```{r}
variant_chr <- rep(c("chr1", "chr2", "chr3"), each = 50)
gene_chr <- rep(c("chr1", "chr2", "chr3"), length.out = ncol(z))
cis <- outer(variant_chr, gene_chr, "==")
W_trans <- w_construction(data_list, exclude = cis)
mean(W_trans == 0)
```

Restricting variants and genes to particular chromosomes (for example a
leave-one-chromosome-out analysis) is done by subsetting the statistics
before building the list.

## Identifying programs with transCCA

`r_transcca()` builds $W$ from the data list with `w_construction()` and fits
a sparse rank-$K$ decomposition of $W$ by penalized matrix decomposition.
Column $k$ of `V` holds the gene loadings of program $k$ and column $k$ of
`U` its variant loadings.

```{r}
prog <- r_transcca(data_list, K = 3, sumabs = 0.4)
prog$d2_score
colSums(prog$V != 0)    # genes per program
```

When `sumabs` is `NULL` (the default), the sparsity level is chosen by
cross-validation. With `different_sparsity = TRUE` it is re-tuned for each
program. Cross-validation is random, so set a seed:

```{r}
set.seed(1)
prog_cv <- r_transcca(data_list, K = 3)
prog_cv$sparsity
```

`exclude`, `tol` and `sig_cut` are passed on to `w_construction()`. Any other
input type works the same way, e.g. individual-level data whitened by the
in-sample expression covariance:

```{r}
set.seed(2)
G <- scale(matrix(rbinom(300 * 20, 2, 0.3), 300, 20,
                  dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("rs", 1:20))))
E <- transmap_example$Y[, 1:30]
E[, 1:12] <- E[, 1:12] + G[, 1]
prog_ind <- r_transcca(list(G = G, E = scale(E), Sigma_EE = "insample"),
                       K = 1, sumabs = 0.4)
prog_ind$input
head(sort(abs(prog_ind$U[, 1]), decreasing = TRUE), 3)
```

## Testing programs against a null

`transcca_null()` simulates data with no variant-gene association
(`generate_null_data()`: genotypes with allele frequencies drawn from the
observed MAF distribution, expression drawn from the gene covariance) and
refits transCCA with the same `K` and `sumabs`. The empirical p-value of a
program is the fraction of null replicates with a larger `d2_score`.

```{r}
set.seed(3)
null <- transcca_null(n_null = 20, n = transmap_example$n, p = nrow(z),
                      maf = runif(1000, 0.05, 0.5),
                      sigma_ee = cor(transmap_example$Y), K = 3,
                      sumabs = 0.4)
transcca_pvalue(prog, null)
```

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
transcca_plot(prog, null, alpha = 0.05)
```

## Building program phenotypes

`transmap_global()` weights the expression of each program's genes by their
loadings. Genes in the program that are missing from the expression matrix
are ignored.

```{r}
glob <- transmap_global(transmap_example$Y, prog)
dim(glob$scores)
head(glob$scores)
```

A plain gene x program loading matrix can be used instead of an
`r_transcca()` result, and covariates can be regressed out of the expression
first:

```{r}
glob_adj <- transmap_global(transmap_example$Y, prog$V,
                            covariates = transmap_example$covariates)
dim(glob_adj$scores)
```
